sources.title: Quran 5:89 (Surah Al-Ma'idah), Quran.com
sources.supports: Allah does not hold you to thoughtless oaths but to deliberate ones; the penalty for a broken oath is feeding ten poor people, clothing them or freeing a slave, and fasting three days for one who cannot afford these.

sources.title: Quran 58:3-4 (Surah Al-Mujadila), Quran.com
sources.supports: Sets the expiation for zihar: free a slave before touching, otherwise fast two consecutive months, otherwise feed sixty needy people.

sources.title: Quran 4:92 (Surah An-Nisa), Quran.com
sources.supports: Gives the expiation for killing a believer by mistake: free a believing slave and pay blood-money, with two consecutive months of fasting for those unable.

sources.title: Quran 2:184 (Surah Al-Baqarah), Quran.com
sources.supports: Allows the ill or travelling to make up fasts later and states a compensation of feeding a needy person for those who can only fast with extreme difficulty.

sources.title: Quran 2:196 (Surah Al-Baqarah), Quran.com
sources.supports: For a pilgrim who is ill or has a scalp ailment requiring shaving, compensation is by fasting, charity or a sacrificial offering.

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari 6622, Sunnah.com
sources.supports: The Prophet told Abdur-Rahman ibn Samura that if he swears an oath and finds something better, he should do the better thing and make expiation for his oath.

sources.title: Sahih Muslim 1650a, Sunnah.com
sources.supports: Whoever swears an oath and finds something better should do it and expiate for the oath; narrated with the case of a man who swore not to eat and then ate.

sources.title: Sahih Muslim 1111a, Sunnah.com
sources.supports: A man who had intercourse with his wife in Ramadan was asked about freeing a slave, fasting two consecutive months and feeding sixty poor people, then was given dates to give to his family.

review.notes: Read each retrieved page. The oath, zihar, mistaken killing, fidyah and pilgrimage verses and the Bukhari and Muslim reports match the paraphrases. No universal cash amount is claimed; scholarly differences are flagged without asserting school positions beyond the sources.

claim_checks.claim: Oath expiation: feed ten, clothe, free a slave, else fast three days
claim_checks.explanation: The 5:89 text lists those options and fasting three days for one who cannot afford them.

claim_checks.claim: Zihar sequence of freeing, fasting two months, feeding sixty
claim_checks.explanation: The 58:3-4 text sets this sequence for those who retract after zihar.

claim_checks.claim: Mistaken killing: free believing slave, blood-money, fast two months if unable
claim_checks.explanation: The 4:92 text states these obligations for unintentional killing.

claim_checks.claim: Fidyah is feeding a needy person for those who can only fast with extreme difficulty
Pilgrim with ailment compensates by fasting, charity or sacrifice
claim_checks.explanation: The 2:196 text states these three options for scalp ailments requiring shaving.

claim_checks.claim: Do the better thing and expiate for the oath
claim_checks.explanation: The Bukhari 6622 Arabic and English text give this instruction to Abdur-Rahman ibn Samura.

claim_checks.claim: Whoever swears and sees better should do it and expiate
claim_checks.explanation: The Muslim 1650a text states this, in the context of a man who swore not to eat.

claim_checks.claim: Ramadan intercourse case: freeing, two months, sixty poor people, dates given
claim_checks.explanation: The Muslim 1111a text gives the Prophet questions in that order and the gift of dates to feed his family.
